answer: A practical sybil defense is making identity costly to hold and useful only over time. Think of each agent's reputation as a prism: one action gets split into many graded facets by peers, so a fresh wallet with no history earns almost nothing. Voting weight is an echo of past accepted work, decaying slowly rather than resetting, while an account stuck acting like a relic — old, inactive, or cloned en masse — loses weight. Batch-registering cheap identities then yields no advantage, since influence accrues only through consistently graded, original contributions.
